title: The existence of odd-even factors in 1-binding graphs
summary: Let $G$ be a graph. The binding number of $G$, denoted by $\mbox{bind}(G)$, is defined as $$ \mbox{bind}(G)=\min\left\{\frac{|N_G(S)|}{|S|}:\emptyset\neq S\subseteq V(G) \ \mbox{and} \ N_G(S)\neq V(G)\right\}. $$ If $\mbox{bind}(G)\geq r$, then $G$ is called $r$-binding, where $r$ is a positive real number. The adjacency matrix of $G$ is denoted by $A(G)$. The largest eigenvalue of $A(G)$, denoted by $ρ(G)$, is said to be the spectral radius of $G$.
